title: Rome Made a Farmer Dictator. He Quit in 16 Days
script: Rome made one farmer dictator for six months. He quit on day sixteen. In 458 BC, an enemy army had trapped a Roman army. The senate sent envoys to a four-acre field across the Tiber. They found Cincinnatus digging a ditch, or ploughing. They saluted him as Dictator. He surrounded the enemy, and they begged for mercy. He sent them under a yoke made of three spears. Then Livy says he resigned, on the sixteenth day, from an office meant to last six months. Six months of power. He took sixteen days.
cta: Follow Hidden Past for the history that got left out.
concept: Reference-led: paper-blue map of Italy with date chip, hex portrait badge, full-bleed period paintings, small word-by-word caption chips, dark circle-portrait beat.
fact_review: 2026-11-26 against facts/26.facts.json. Year 458 BC: Wikipedia gives '458 or 457 BC' (f1); script says 458 BC, the date Wikipedia lists first. 'Trapped' attributed via Wikipedia citing Livy III.26. Ploughing/ditch and four-acre field: Livy 3.26 (Roberts). Dictator salute: 3.26. Yoke of three spears and supplication: 3.28. Sixteenth day and six months: 3.29. Wikipedia's own text also says 'fifteen days' in one sentence; the script follows Livy's 'sixteenth day'. 'Farmer' is the video's shorthand for 'cultivated a four-acre field' (3.26).
